title: Quote route crashes with a raw yfinance internal exception for an actively-traded, correctly-resolvable SME listing
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/quotes/SUMAX?asset_class=equity -> HTTP 502 {"detail": "yfinance quote failed for 'SUMAX': 'PriceHistory' object has no attribute '_dividends'"}
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P15_SUMAX.json:138-149 (502 body); cross-checked against docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P15_SUMAX.json:127-141 (price.last_close 114.50 INR, day_range, volume 79,200, circuit_limits, all sourced 2026-09-18 from groww.in/indmoney.com corroborating each other)
notes: Mechanism: SUMAX listed 2026-09-02 (12 trading sessions old) and has no dividend history at all -- the raw AttributeError ('PriceHistory' object has no attribute '_dividends') strongly implies the yfinance quote path unconditionally touches a dividends accessor that is only populated for tickers with an existing corporate-action/dividend series, and a brand-new listing with zero dividend history breaks that assumption; the library's internal exception is surfaced verbatim as the API's 502 detail instead of being caught and degraded. Consequence: the single most basic panel (live price, day range, volume, circuit limits) is completely unavailable for a real, currently-trading NSE Emerge instrument -- worse, the raw provider-internal error string leaks straight to the client, which is also an information-hygiene smell. Smallest fix shape: catch AttributeError (and any yfinance internal shape-error) around the dividends/PriceHistory access in the quote path and degrade to a partial quote (price/volume without a dividends field) rather than a hard 502; add a regression case for a newly-listed, dividend-free scrip.

title: Fundamentals route returns a completely unrelated foreign entity's blank record under symbol 'SUMAX' -- wrong identity, not just missing data
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/SUMAX -> {"symbol": "SUMAX", "name": "SEI Short Duration Municipal F (STET)", "sector": null, "industry": null, ...} with every substantive field null (market_cap, pe_ratio, price_to_book, roe, debt_to_equity, revenue_ttm, net_income_ttm, revenue_growth, eps, book_value, dividend_yield, dividend_per_share_ttm, fifty_two_week_high, fifty_two_week_low all null).
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P15_SUMAX.json:150-204 (full body, name field at :156); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/diffs/P15_SUMAX.json (17 fields rolled up under this finding: identity.board/sector/industry/listing_date, market_cap, pe_ttm, pb, roe, roce, debt_to_equity, revenue_ttm, net_profit_ttm, revenue_growth_yoy, eps_ttm, book_value_per_share, dividend.paid_trailing_12m_per_share, dividend.yield, week52.high, week52.low -- all 'app blank' against sourced outside values in docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P15_SUMAX.json); resolve endpoint's own correct candidate at collected/P15_SUMAX.json:23-24 ('SUMAX ENGINEERING LIMITED', NSE) shows the app HAS the right identity available and did not use it here
notes: Mechanism: '/resolve?q=SUMAX' correctly surfaces the real company (SUMAX ENGINEERING LIMITED, NSE Emerge SME) as a candidate but returns needs_disambiguation=true without auto-confirming it; the fundamentals route was then called with the raw unresolved 'SUMAX' string, which some downstream provider (openbb-mcp per the 'provider' field, ultimately backed by a symbol lookup) matched to an entirely unrelated instrument -- 'SEI Short Duration Municipal F (STET)', a US municipal bond mutual fund -- and returned that fund's (empty) record under the SUMAX symbol key. This is not an honest blank: the payload actively asserts a wrong company name for the requested symbol. Consequence: this is exactly the data-trust failure the product's stated moat depends on (COMMON.md: 'the moat is data trust') -- a user or an agent reading body.name would conclude either that SUMAX has been renamed to an unrelated US fund, or (if the name is ignored downstream) simply that no fundamentals exist, for reasons that have nothing to do with the real cause (unresolved symbol handoff between /resolve and /fundamentals). Smallest fix shape: /fundamentals must consume the resolved (disambiguated) instrument -- exchange/region-qualified symbol (e.g. SUMAX-SM.NS or equivalent) -- from /resolve rather than re-resolving the bare query string against a provider with no exchange/region scoping; when the provider match confidence is low or the returned name doesn't match the requested company, refuse and surface an explicit unresolved-identity error instead of the wrong entity's blank record.

title: Every disclosures route (shareholding, announcements, results) 502s for a real, correctly-identified listing -- the mandatory subtle-tier fields (promoter/FII/DII/public shareholding) are wholly unavailable
repro: GET .../disclosures/shareholding?symbol=SUMAX -> 502 "disclosures: 'SUMAX' is not a known NSE/BSE instrument"; GET .../disclosures/announcements?symbol=SUMAX&limit=25 -> same 502; GET .../disclosures/results?symbol=SUMAX -> 502 "nse_direct: 'SUMAX' is not a known NSE instrument"
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P15_SUMAX.json:272-307 (all three 502 bodies); outside cross-check docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P15_SUMAX.json:317-334 (shareholding: promoter 69.67%, FII 2.10%, DII 9.59%, public 18.63%, 1074 shareholders, screener.in-sourced), :410-435 (3 recent NSE-filed announcements, 2026-09-09 to 2026-09-11), :356-374 (Q1 FY2027 results: revenue 35.68cr, PAT 3.50cr, filed 2026-09-08)
notes: Mechanism: same unresolved-instrument class of failure as DAT-P15-1/DAT-P15-2 -- every disclosures route treats the bare 'SUMAX' string as an unknown instrument rather than routing through the resolver's own correct candidate. Consequence is more severe than a generic blank: PROMPT_data_s2.md's own mandatory subtle tier singles out shareholding/promoter/FII/DII as 'the single most gameable number in an Indian small-cap' -- for this listing that entire tier is not degraded, it is 100% absent, alongside the announcements feed (which would have surfaced the 2026-09-24/09-30 AGM book closure) and the results calendar (Q1 FY27 numbers, filed two weeks before this collection). For a 17-day-old SME listing where the shareholding pattern is the freshest, highest-signal data available (first post-listing disclosure, anchor-investor allotments still visible), the app shows nothing at all. Smallest fix shape: same as DAT-P15-2 -- disclosures routes need to accept/derive the exchange-qualified resolved symbol rather than assuming a bare uppercase string is directly usable against nse_direct/BSE lookups, with an explicit degrade-and-explain path (not a raw 502 with an internal provider error string) when a real listing genuinely has no disclosures yet.

title: face_value (par value) has no representation anywhere in the app's fundamentals/identity schema
repro: GET /resolve?q=SUMAX and GET /fundamentals/SUMAX -> neither response, nor any other field in the schema, contains a face_value/par-value key.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P15_SUMAX.json:11-41 (resolve body, full field list), :150-199 (fundamentals body, full field list, no face_value key); outside cross-check docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P15_SUMAX.json:260-266 (face_value 10.0 INR, screener.in, corroborated by Groww)
notes: Mechanism: this is a schema-level gap, not specific to SUMAX or to the unresolved-symbol issue above -- there is simply no face_value concept anywhere in the Indian-equity fundamentals response. Consequence: low severity on its own, but matters for interpreting split/bonus-adjusted prices and per-share ratios correctly, and for SUMAX specifically it would flag the coincidence noted in the pack (52-week low 101.20 visually collides with the issue price 101, both near the INR 10 face value's usual round-number peers). Smallest fix shape: source face_value from the BSE/NSE ComHeadernew-equivalent feed the app already uses for other identity fields, once the resolver-handoff issue (DAT-P15-2) is fixed enough to reach that feed at all for this symbol.

title: Company-name search cannot find the company by its own exact legal name, even though bare-symbol search can
repro: GET /resolve?q=Sumax+Engineering+Ltd -> needs_disambiguation:true with SIX candidates (SMT Engineering Ltd, DMR Engineering Ltd, Misquita Engineering Ltd, Duncan Engineering Ltd, Shayona Engineering Ltd, Ajax Engineering Limited) -- none of which is Sumax Engineering. GET /resolve?q=SUMAX (bare symbol) DOES surface 'SUMAX ENGINEERING LIMITED' as its sole candidate.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P15_SUMAX.json:42-131 (company-name query, 6 wrong candidates), contrast with :11-41 (bare-symbol query, correct single candidate); outside cross-check docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P15_SUMAX.json:7-13 (legal_name confirmed as 'Sumax Engineering Limited'/'Ltd' across screener.in, groww.in, indmoney.com)
notes: Mechanism: the free-text/company-name resolution path appears to rank on generic token overlap ('Engineering', 'Ltd') rather than weighting the more specific and rarer token ('Sumax') highly enough to surface the actual target -- for a listing 17 days old at collection time, this reads as a name-search index that has not picked up the new entity at all, with the fuzzy matcher papering over the miss by returning plausible-looking but entirely wrong 'Engineering Ltd' companies instead of an honest zero-results state. Consequence: a user or an agent typing the company's own full legal name -- the single most natural way to look up a stock -- gets six confident-looking wrong answers and no indication that the real company was never in the candidate set, which is worse than the bare-symbol path's honest (if unresolved) 'needs disambiguation' with the correct company present. This is a core discovery-flow break for any name just added to the exchange. Smallest fix shape: when a full-text company-name query has zero token overlap on the most distinctive term(s) with any of its top candidates, either omit those candidates or flag the result set as low-confidence/possibly-incomplete rather than presenting six same-shaped 'Engineering Ltd' names as equally plausible matches; audit whether the name-search index has a lag against newly-listed NSE Emerge names distinct from the symbol-lookup index (which clearly does have SUMAX).
